question: Assume today is 2026-08-29. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of people who moved between municipalities within Japan in August 2026 (Japanese and foreign residents combined), as first reported in the Statistics Bureau of Japan's monthly Report on Internal Migration in Japan Derived from the Basic Resident Registration.

target.what: Number of persons who changed their municipality of residence within Japan (inter-municipal/internal migration moves) during August 2026, as recorded in the Statistics Bureau of Japan's monthly Report on Internal Migration in Japan Derived from the Basic Resident Registration (住民基本台帳人口移動報告), countin
target.publisher: Statistics Bureau of Japan (総務省統計局), Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications
target.cadence: monthly (preliminary figures released roughly 3-4 weeks after month end; August 2026 report would normally publish around late September 2026, i.e., after the cutoff)
target.caveats: Working interpretation: the target is the monthly total of internal migration moves (transfers between municipalities) reported in the Basic Resident Registration-based report, combining Japanese and foreign residents, for the calendar month August 2026. Key definitional issues: (1) the report count

candidates.hypothesis: The August 2026 total is best anchored on the same month in prior years (August 2023, 2024, 2025) plus the most recent published months before the cutoff (e.g., Jan-Jul 2026), since internal migration has strong seasonality (August is a peak moving month) and a stable level with modest year-over-year drift. Target = prior August level × (1 + recent YoY growth).
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly total internal migration moves (Japanese + foreign combined, and separately Japanese-only and foreign-only) for August 2023, August 2024, August 2025, and all months of 2025 and Jan-Jul 2026 from the Report on Internal Migration (住民基本台帳人口移動報告). Minimum: August values for the last 3 years and the latest 6-12 monthly totals.

methods.label: m1

a1.role: August 2026 all-person level relative to August 2024

methods.rationale: Direct seasonal anchor: the same calendar month two years earlier, carried forward by a small drift factor reflecting the near-flat annual trend plus the rising foreign component. Failure mode: the drift factor is an assumption; if 2026 migration deviates sharply from the stable 2024-2025 trend this route is off.

methods.label: m2

a1.role: August 2026 all-person level relative to August 2024

methods.rationale: Same anchor as m1 but expressed as a sum of Japanese and foreign components: the all-person August 2024 level times the drift factor, with the foreign share a2 used only to verify the split is consistent with the rising foreign trend. Shared dependency with m1 (same p50 and a1); this is a structural cross-check, not independent confirmation.

excluded_by_input_audit.label: m3
excluded_by_input_audit.reason: input audit: p1: July 2026 Japanese-only movers is a different period than the target August 2026; the ratio a3 is a combined-total adjustment, not a per-component period bridge, and the role states July.; p4: July 2026 foreign-only movers is a different period than the target August 2026.

kept.applies_when: Used to carry the August 2024 all-person level forward to August 2026.
kept.falsified_by: Published 2026 monthly data showing a sharp (>5%) annual change in the all-person total.

kept.name: August 2026 foreign share of all-person inter-municipal moves
kept.rationale: Foreign share was ~11.8% in August 2024 (42,009/355,918), ~15.2% in October 2025, and ~12.8% for 2025 annually; the share is trending up, so August 2026 should sit above the August 2024 value, near 13-14%.
kept.applies_when: Used to split the August 2026 all-person total into Japanese and foreign components for the sum method.
kept.falsified_by: Published foreign share for mid-2026 outside 11.5-16%.

kept.name: August 2026 combined total relative to July 2026 combined total
kept.rationale: August 2024 (355,918) was below October 2025 (379,751) and the July 2026 combined level is ~390,799; August is not reliably a strong peak, so a near-unity ratio with wide range is appropriate rather than a large uplift.
kept.applies_when: Used to scale the July 2026 combined level to August 2026.
kept.falsified_by: Published August/July ratios consistently outside 0.90-1.15 in prior years.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
